body:
N-40, SECOND NOTE (26 Nov 2026, lead; after the advisor's read of the first). (1) WORDING CORRECTION to the first note: 'not even the file in flight finished' is an INFERENCE. Bytes were counted, not files: after the swipe 0.27 MB arrived, which could be the tail of one nearly-finished file. The fact is: at most part of one song arrived; files completed were inferred from bytes, not counted.

(2) READING 1 (advisor): what the Samsung swipe does to the package, read on the A35 at 10:08:47 UTC during a second swipe mid-download: `stopped=false` for user 0 (it is NOT a force-stop; the package keeps its scheduled work), the process is GONE, and `dumpsys jobscheduler` lists exactly ONE job of the app: the WorkManager system job `androidx.work.systemjobscheduler:u0a60/11487`, RUNNABLE but waiting for its time ('TIME=+2h7m', network and battery-not-low constraints; its history shows a run every few hours: the background sync). So nothing restarted in the 3 minutes because NOTHING WAS SCHEDULED for the downloads: the downloader's work lives and dies with the process; no job, alarm or service of the app is there to bring it back.

(3) READ IN THE PLUGIN (background_downloader 9.6.4, doc/CONFIG.md and doc/lifecycle.md; not run): (a) `Config.runInForeground` runs a task as a foreground service ONLY when the task has a `running` notification configured; API 34+ needs `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC` and `androidx.work.impl.foreground.SystemForegroundService` with `foregroundServiceType="dataSync"` in the manifest (the app has only the mediaPlayback type today); (b) the plugin's own `holdingQueue` lives on the NATIVE side and 'tasks continue to get pulled from it when the app is suspended', unlike the Dart `TaskQueue`; the app's manager feeds at most `maxInFlight = 4` files from Dart, so a process kept alive by a foreground service would still starve once the Dart side is gone unless the whole queue is handed to the native holding queue; (c) the replay on reopen exists (`trackTasks`, `resumeFromBackground`, already called by the transport's `resume`). The transport comment 'what survives the app being killed is only the files already handed over' is FALSE as measured: the native worker dies with the process.

(4) READING 2 (advisor): a throwaway spike (foreground mode + notification + holding queue of 4 + maxInFlight raised, in the local worktree wt-spike40, script scratchpad/spike40.py; NEVER pushed) was started and its APK build was STOPPED by the system for low memory (not a failure). NOT RUN YET. It answers whether a process held by a foreground service survives a One UI swipe and whether the Dart isolate survives with it. Start it again only when asked or when memory allows; install it over build 162 (same versionCode, adb install -r), repeat the swipe and the byte count, then reinstall the real build 162 from releases-archive/build-162-b575189/. The phone still holds a full download of '00s Hip Hop (188 of 189 when its re-download finishes).
